conventions: stop entries mechanized as signal-bar-close then next-bar-open; every tunable constant is a parameter; long side only in pseudocode (bear mirror per Brooks). swingHigh(n)/swingLow(n) = the n-th most recent confirmed swing pivot per the T17-01 pivotStrength-bar confirmation definition.

candidates.name: ExpandingTrianglePrimitive
candidates.quote: An expanding triangle can be either a reversal or a continuation pattern and is made of at least five swings (sometimes seven, and rarely nine), each one greater than the prior one.
candidates.description: Primitive: at least five alternating swing pivots, each extending further than the swing two pivots back on the same side (progressively higher highs AND progressively lower lows) - the opposite of a wedge's convergence.
candidates.pseudocode: isExpandingTriangle(pivotStrength, minLegs) = forall k in 1..minLegs-2: swingHigh(k) > swingHigh(k+2) && swingLow(k) < swingLow(k+2)
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (pattern classification used as a precondition for other candidates in this file)

complexity.reason: needs swing-pivot detection (T17-01's pivotStrength-bar confirmation) and a comparison of alternating highs and lows across at least five pivots

notes: Same underlying primitive as ExpandingTriangleTopBottom (VP1-17), defined independently per chapter per convention; dedup pass should merge.

Unlike a wedge, this pattern is direction-agnostic in shape (both extremes diverge), so 'same' rather than 'mirrored' at the classification level; the reversal/continuation trades built on it are directional and mirrored.

candidates.name: ExpandingTriangleInitialTarget
candidates.quote: The initial target is a breakout beyond the opposite side of the triangle, where the market often tries to reverse again... in most cases, that is as far as the trade goes.
candidates.description: For a reversal trade out of an expanding triangle, the first (and usually only) target is a new extreme just beyond the opposite side of the pattern from where the entry triggered - i.e., beyond the most recent opposing swing pivot.
candidates.pseudocode:
initialTarget = swingHigh(1); // for a long reversal off an expanding triangle bottom, target the pattern's own opposite (high) side
exitLongAtTarget = high[0] >= initialTarget
candidates.book_order_type: limit exit (or discretionary scale-out) at the opposite side of the triangle

complexity.reason: the target is the pattern's own most recent opposing pivot, so it inherits V06-01's swing-pivot detection

candidates.name: ExpandingTriangleLastLegMeasuredMove
candidates.quote: If the breakout succeeds, then the next objective in the reversal down is a measured move that is approximately the same height as the last leg up in the triangle.
candidates.description: If price breaks beyond the initial target (V06-02), the next target is a measured move equal in size to the pattern's own last (opposing) leg, projected beyond the initial target.
candidates.pseudocode:
lastLegHeight = swingHigh(1) - swingLow(1); // the most recent leg of the triangle, opposite the trade direction
secondTarget = initialTarget - lastLegHeight; // for a short reversal off an expanding triangle top
exitShortAtSecondTarget = low[0] <= secondTarget
candidates.book_order_type: limit exit (or discretionary scale-out) at the measured-move price

complexity.reason: the leg boundaries are pivot-derived (V06-01), and the target additionally chains off V06-02's initial target

notes: Uses the LAST LEG's height specifically, not the full pattern height - distinct from V05-02's wedge-height target.

candidates.name: ExpandingTriangleFailedReversalBecomesFlag
candidates.quote: If the breakout fails and the market reverses up, then the triangle becomes a continuation pattern, which in this case would be an expanding triangle bull flag... The initial target would be a new high, and usually that is about as far as the trade goes.
candidates.description: If the reversal breakout out of an expanding triangle fails to reach V06-02's initial target and price instead reverses back toward the original (pre-pattern) trend direction, trade the pattern as a with-trend continuation flag instead: enter with-trend on the reversal back, targeting a new extreme in the trend direction.
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop above the reversal-back signal bar's high

complexity.reason: requires the same pivot detection as V06-01 plus a 'reversal failed' test that is itself only loosely defined (no explicit price level given for when a countertrend attempt is deemed to have failed)

candidates.name: ExpandingTriangleContinuationMeasuredMove
candidates.quote: If the breakout succeeds, the next target is a measured move up that is about the size of the last leg down in the triangle.
candidates.description: For the continuation-flag trade (V06-04), once the initial new-extreme target is reached, the next target is a measured move equal to the pattern's own last (against-continuation) leg, projected beyond that extreme.
candidates.book_order_type: limit exit (or discretionary scale-out) at the measured-move price

complexity.reason: same pivot-derived leg height as V06-03, chained off V06-04's continuation target

notes: Mirror-image counterpart of V06-03: same arithmetic, opposite trade direction.

candidates.name: ExpandingTriangleGrowsLegsOnRepeatedFailure
candidates.quote: If the breakout fails and the market turns down, it is now a larger expanding triangle top with seven legs instead of the original five. At some point, either a breakout succeeds and the market makes an approximate measured move or the triangle evolves into a larger trading range.
candidates.description: Each time a reversal/continuation breakout attempt out of an expanding triangle fails, the pattern grows by two legs (five to seven, seven to nine) and the same reversal/continuation logic (V06-02 through V06-05) is re-applied at the larger scale.
candidates.pseudocode:
// recursive re-application of V06-01..V06-05 with minLegs incremented by 2 each time a breakout attempt fails
isLargerExpandingTriangle = isExpandingTriangle(pivotStrength, minLegs + 2)
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (pattern-growth classification, not a distinct order)

complexity.reason: recursive pattern re-evaluation over a growing pivot count; same swing-pivot mechanics as V06-01 but with an unbounded leg count

notes: Practically this just means minLegs should be treated as a lower bound, not an exact count, when checking V06-01 on later bars.

candidates.name: ExpandingTriangleReversalRequiresPriorTrendLineBreak
candidates.quote: At a minimum, the rally from the second push down breaks above the bear trend line that contained that second leg down, and the third push down is therefore a lower low major trend reversal buy setup.
candidates.description: An expanding-triangle reversal is only valid as a major trend reversal if an earlier leg of the pattern already broke the trend line that contained the prior trend - i.e., the pattern requires a prior trend-line break, not just the diverging-swings shape alone.
candidates.pseudocode:
priorTrendLineBroken = trendLineBrokenWithin(lookbackBars);
isValidTrianglePatternReversal = isExpandingTriangle(pivotStrength, minLegs) && priorTrendLineBroken;

complexity.reason: needs trend-line projection from pivots (to detect the break) in addition to V06-01's pivot detection

notes: Same underlying requirement as TrendLineBreakBeforeReversal (V01-01) / TrendLineBreakRequiredForReversal (VP1-01), applied specifically to the expanding-triangle shape.

candidates.name: ExpandingTrianglePartialScalpEachLeg
candidates.quote: There are usually valid reasons to scalp each leg (for example, each leg is a new swing high or low in a trading range), but once the fifth leg is complete, a larger trend can develop and it is wise to swing part of the position.
candidates.description: While an expanding triangle is still forming (before the minimum leg count completes), scalp each new swing extreme rather than holding for a larger move; once the pattern's minimum leg count completes, hold part of the position for a potential larger trend instead of scalping it all.

complexity.reason: needs a running count of completed pivots against the pattern's own leg boundaries

rejected.quote: It was similar to a ninth leg of an expanding triangle (in trading, similar is usually good enough).
rejected.reason: pure discretion ('similar is good enough'), no bar-level tolerance given for how similar counts

rejected.quote: When the shape is that unconventional, fewer traders will trust it and that weakens the pattern.

chapter_summary: Chapter 6 treats the expanding triangle as a five-(sometimes seven or nine)-leg variant of the three-push family (V06-01, diverging rather than converging), with the same target structure as a wedge but using the pattern's LAST LEG height (not full pattern height) for its measured move (V06-02/03). Every reversal attempt can fail and flip into a with-trend continuation flag with its own initial target and measured move (V06-04/05), and repeated failures simply grow the pattern by two legs at a time (V06-06). A valid reversal additionally requires a prior trend-line break (V06-07, restating V01-01/VP1-01 for this shape), and management calls for scalping each leg while the pattern is still forming but holding a runner once the minimum leg count completes (V06-08). The chapter is otherwise entirely worked chart examples (Figures 6.1-6.3, bar-numbered); no additional general rules were found in the annotations beyond what is captured above.
